name: Norway
tagline: Free, close to Denmark — and almost entirely in Norwegian
summary: Norway charges EU/EEA students no tuition, and your IB converts generously onto the Norwegian scale. The catch is language: NTNU, UiT and several other big universities teach every bachelor's degree in Norwegian, and only about fifteen bachelor's programmes nationally are in English. But Samordna opptak counts Danish A at grade 3 or better as documented Norwegian, so if you take Danish A (or Norwegian or Swedish A) you can apply to the whole free Norwegian-taught system through one application with ten ranked choices, closing 15 April.
whyConsider: No tuition at public institutions for EU/EEA citizens — you pay only a semester fee of roughly NOK 850–1,000.
Danish, Norwegian or Swedish A at grade 3 or better, HL or SL, meets Samordna opptak's Norwegian requirement, so if you take one of them no Norwegian test is needed for Norwegian-taught programmes.
If you can claim Danish SU, it is paid here as if you studied in Denmark, not capped at the four years that apply outside the Nordics.
IB Maths AA SL on its own satisfies the Norwegian R1+R2 requirement, so engineering needs only Physics SL alongside it.
43–45 IB points converts to 60.0 karakterpoeng — the top of the Norwegian scale.
Genuinely distinctive niches: Arctic and marine biology at Nord, game development at INN, sport science at NIH.
watchOuts: NTNU, UiT and HVL state plainly that they offer no English-taught bachelor's degrees. UiB's three English-listed 'bachelors' are Norwegian-language degrees.
English-taught programmes apply direct to the institution and often close on 1 December 2026 — months before Danish or British norms, and before predicted grades are settled.

UiO's one English-taught bachelor's wants every document by 1 December 2026, which a May 2027 candidate cannot meet. NMBU's is open to you through Samordna opptak by 15 April if you document Norwegian, and Danish, Norwegian or Swedish A does.
The Samordna opptak documentation deadline of 1 July falls before IB results are released on 6 July. You must arrange the IBO Request for Results Service with your IB coordinator.
Unless you hold Norwegian citizenship, Lånekassen is realistically closed to a school-leaver arriving from Denmark, and Norway offers no scholarships to EU/EEA bachelor students.
Living costs are high: the official student budget is NOK 15,488 per month, roughly €1,320.

ibRecognition.minimumPoints: No minimum point score for a full IB Diploma holder — holding the Diploma is itself the education requirement. A DP Course Results / IB Certificate needs at least 20 points including TOK/EE points, passed TOK and Extended Essay, completed CAS, and grade 3 or better in all subjects, with 3 SL + 3 HL or 2 SL + 4 HL.
ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: Grade 3 or better is required in each subject used to meet a specific requirement. Mathematical Studies SL and Maths AI SL cover S1+S2. Maths AA SL, AA HL and AI HL all cover R1+R2. Physics SL covers Fysikk 1 and Physics HL covers Fysikk 1+2; the same SL/HL pattern applies to Chemistry, Biology, Computer Science, Economics and Design Technology.
ibRecognition.gradeConversion: Total points (the 45-point scale, including TOK/EE bonus points) converts to Norwegian karakterpoeng: 43–45 = 60.0, 42 = 59.3, 41 = 58.6, 40 = 57.1, 38 = 54.3, 35 = 50.0, 32 = 45.7, 30 = 42.9, 28 = 40.0, 24 = 34.3, 20 = 26.0. The table is set by the Ministry of Education (Kunnskapsdepartementet). Up to 4 language and science points are added on top for qualifying subjects at grade 3 or better.
notes: Maths AA SL alone satisfies R1+R2, which works strongly in an IB student's favour. In the Danish system the equivalent normally means Matematik A.
IB English at grade 3 or better satisfies the national English requirement — no IELTS or TOEFL needed.

The Norwegian language requirement does not apply to programmes taught in English (opptaksforskrifta § 3-8). Institutions do not apply this uniformly, though: NMBU requires Norwegian B2 for its English-taught bachelor's when you apply through Samordna opptak — which Danish, Norwegian or Swedish A at grade 3 documents.

Settled: Samordna opptak's IB page lists Danish A, higher or standard level, at grade 3 or better as meeting the Norwegian requirement for general admission, alongside Norwegian A and Swedish A. If you take Danish, Norwegian or Swedish A and reach grade 3, you do not need Norskprøven or Bergenstesten.
Also unconfirmed: whether an IB Diploma earned abroad counts as a førstegangsvitnemål for the reserved quota. This materially affects how competitive you are.

deadlines.label: University of Oslo — Technology Systems: Science and Engineering, applicants without Norwegian
deadlines.notes: UiO's own admission page for applicants who cannot document Norwegian proficiency. UiO states "You must submit all documents before the application deadline, or your application will not be considered", so a May 2027 IB candidate cannot document the Diploma in time: this route suits a student who already holds it. The financing documentation the page demands does not apply to Norwegian, Nordic and EU/EEA citizens.

deadlines.label: NMBU — International Environment and Development Studies, applicants without Norwegian
deadlines.notes: Published as "1 December, the year before you plan to start" — but only for applicants "from outside the Nordic countries" who "cannot document proficiency in Norwegian". If you take Danish, Norwegian or Swedish A and reach grade 3 or better, you document Norwegian and apply through Samordna opptak by 15 April instead, where NMBU requires Norwegian B2 even though the programme is taught in English. Without one of those, this 1 December route is the one.

deadlines.label: University of Agder — music performance programmes (Classical Music Performance, Electronic Music)
deadlines.notes: Published as "Application deadline for all applicants to music performance programmes" on 15 December, with no year; the year is inferred from the intake this profile covers. Two of UiA's four English-taught bachelor's are music performance degrees, so for them the deadline is December, not 1 March.

deadlines.label: Samordna opptak opens for the 2027 admission round
deadlines.year: 2027 entry — 2027 calendar not yet published; 2026 pattern shown
deadlines.notes: Published as "Opent for søking" on 1 February, when the study overview for the round is also released. Nothing can be submitted through Samordna opptak before this day, and the same 1 February opening applies to the University of Agder's and Nord's own English-taught application webs.

deadlines.label: NHH Norwegian School of Economics — BSc in Business, Economics and Data Science, EU/EEA/Swiss
deadlines.notes: NHH publishes "1 January – 15 February 2027: Submit application, test results, and diploma." If you are eligible for a conditional offer, official predicted grades are due by 15 February 2027 and the final diploma can be uploaded later, until 6 July 2027. Decisions for the EU/EEA/Swiss round come in May. Non-EU/EEA/Swiss applicants apply 1–15 November 2026.

deadlines.label: University of Agder — English-taught bachelor's except music performance, EU/EEA applicants
deadlines.notes: UiA's date, published as "Application deadline for EU/EEA applicants" with no year, so the year is inferred from the intake this profile covers. It covers Academic Esports and English; the two music performance degrees close earlier, on 15 December (their own entry). UiA's application web opens 1 February, and results for EU/EEA applicants come on 1 June and 10 July.

deadlines.label: Samordna opptak main deadline (Norwegian-taught programmes)
deadlines.year: 2027 entry — 2027 calendar not yet published; 2026 pattern shown
deadlines.notes: Published as "15. april kl. 23.59 er siste frist for å søkje". Up to ten ranked choices. The round opens on 1 February, which has its own entry. Documentation for a regular applicant is due the same day, with the exception for spring-semester results that pushes the upload to 1 July.

deadlines.label: Nord University — English-taught bachelor's, EU/EEA and Nordic applicants
deadlines.notes: Published as the window "1 February - 15 April" with no year, so the year here is inferred from the intake this profile covers. The application itself is due on this date; the educational documentation has a later deadline of its own, which is the next entry. Nord publishes results to EU/EEA applicants at the beginning of July. The dates are on Nord's central admission page, not on the programme pages.

deadlines.label: Nord University — documentation deadline for spring school-leavers
deadlines.notes: Nord's general rule is that EU/EEA applicants document by 15 April, but applicants who finish secondary school in the spring — which every May-session IB candidate does — have until 1 July to upload their educational documentation. Published without a year, so the year here is inferred from the intake this profile covers. It falls on the same day as the Samordna opptak documentation deadline and, like that one, before IB results are released, so the same Request for Results arrangement applies.

deadlines.label: Samordna opptak documentation deadline
deadlines.notes: Falls before IB results are released on 6 July. Samordna opptak's answer for a student graduating this year: you will not be able to upload your diploma by 1 July, so fill in the IB's "Request for Results Service" with your IB coordinator, naming the institutions that handle your application, and they read your results electronically. This is also the omprioriteringsfrist, the last day on which you can reorder your ranked choices.

deadlines.label: Samordna opptak results published
deadlines.notes: The main admission result. Applications for vacant places (ledige studieplassar) open the same day. What you do next has its own entry and its own deadline, four days later.

deadlines.label: Accept or decline your Samordna opptak offer
deadlines.year: 2027 entry — 2027 calendar not yet published; 2026 pattern shown
deadlines.notes: Published as "Siste frist for å svare", at 23:59. Put it in a calendar the day you apply, not the day you are offered a place.

steps: Decide early whether you are applying in English or in Norwegian — they are two different systems with different deadlines, and you can use both.
For English-taught programmes, apply directly to each institution through its Søknadsweb portal. Check each deadline individually; they range from 1 December 2026 to 15 April 2027.

For Norwegian-taught programmes, register on Samordna opptak from 1 February 2027 and list up to ten choices in order of preference. A lower choice is dropped automatically once a higher one is offered.

Ask your IB coordinator to fill in the IB's Request for Results Service in spring 2027, naming the institutions that handle your application, so they can read your results electronically — the 1 July documentation deadline falls before results day.
Upload your IB diploma and transcript. No translation is needed for documents in English or a Scandinavian language.

If you are a Nordic citizen, you do not register with the police. Other EU/EEA citizens staying more than three months register with the police within three months of arriving. If you will stay more than six months, report your move to Norway to the Tax Administration (Skatteetaten) to get a national identity number.
application.selectionNotes: Two quotas: a first-time-certificate quota competing on skolepoeng, and an ordinary quota competing on konkurransepoeng (which adds age points and up to two supplementary points). For autumn 2027 the procedural reforms bite — særskilt vurdering is abolished, ties are broken by lottery, and institutions may introduce their own ranking entrance tests — but age points, the current supplementary-point regime and the 50% first-time quota all survive. The bigger changes, including the removal of age points entirely, land in 2028.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: Very limited — roughly fifteen programmes nationally. HK-dir lists 361 English-taught programmes across all levels, but these are overwhelmingly master's.
language.englishProof: IB English (A or B) at grade 3 or better satisfies the national requirement, as does English being your language of instruction. The national floor for test-takers is IELTS 5.0 or TOEFL iBT 60, but individual programmes set higher bars.
notes: Norwegian is not required for programmes taught in English, but it is required for everything else — which is most of the system.
Norwegian B2 can be documented through Norskprøven (B2 in all four skills) or Bergenstesten.

Danish and Norwegian are mutually intelligible in writing, so reaching B2 Norwegian is a far smaller undertaking for a Danish speaker than for most applicants. This is worth taking seriously — it unlocks the whole free system.

tuitionEuEea.value: None at public institutions. BI Norwegian Business School is private and charges NOK 106,400 per year even to EU/EEA students.

tuitionNonEu.value: Mandatory but no longer required to be cost-covering since 1 August 2026. Several institutions cut fees sharply: Nord and UiS now NOK 60,000–85,000, INN NOK 68,000, USN NOK 50,000–90,000. NTNU, UiO, UiB and HVL did not cut. UiO's 2027/28 rates are NOK 218,000 for science and technology and NOK 186,000 for humanities and social science.

livingCostMonthly.value: NOK 15,488 per month (about €1,320), or NOK 170,368 per year

notes: Every student pays a semester fee of about NOK 1,000 per semester to the student welfare organisation. It buys the student ID, discounted transport, health services and gym access, and you cannot sit exams without it.

The figure of NOK 15,488 per month is formally the immigration authority's subsistence requirement for non-EEA students, but it is also the realistic cost of living and the right number for you to budget against.

funding.note: In 2026 it is DKK 7,426 a month before tax if you live away from your parents. Because Norway is a Nordic country, it is paid as if you studied in Denmark — for anyone starting after 1 July 2025, for the programme's prescribed length only. It uses SU-klip, within the 70-klip frame su.dk sets for all higher education abroad.

funding: Lånekassen, the Norwegian loan fund, requires either permanent residence, five years in Norway, or worker status with at least ten hours a week alongside your studies. A 19-year-old arriving straight from gymnasium does not qualify — though taking a part-time job is a genuine route in.
There are no Norwegian government scholarships for EU/EEA bachelor students. Study in Norway says so outright.
workRights: No restriction for EU/EEA students. Non-EU students on a first-time permit may work 20 hours a week during term and full-time in holidays.
residency: No residence permit is needed. If you are a Nordic citizen, you do not register with the police either; other EU/EEA citizens staying more than three months register with the police within three months of arriving. If you will stay more than six months, report your move to Norway to the Tax Administration (Skatteetaten); once it is approved you receive a national identity number.
housing: Run by the Samskipnad (student welfare organisation) in each city — SiO in Oslo — and funded by the semester fee. Applications are accepted year-round and offers go out continuously. Oslo, Bergen and Trondheim all have shortages at the August intake, and Oslo's private market is the main reason Norway is expensive despite free tuition. Apply the day your offer arrives.
healthcare: Bring your EHIC. It covers medically necessary care from public providers on the same terms as a tourist. Once you are registered as resident with a national identity number you get care on the same basis as Norwegians, including a fastlege (assigned GP). Helsenorge recommends private insurance on top, particularly for repatriation. Taking a job generally makes you a member of folketrygden — check with NAV.

institutions.name: University of Agder
institutions.englishBachelors: 4 — Academic Esports (Grimstad), Classical Music Performance, Electronic Music, English
institutions.note: A public university with four English-taught bachelor's to choose from. Academic Esports and English close on 1 March for EU/EEA applicants; the two music degrees close on 15 December.

institutions.name: BI Norwegian Business School
institutions.englishBachelors: 3 — Business Administration (BBA), Data Science for Business, Digital Business
institutions.note: Three English-taught business bachelor's, triple-crown accredited — but private, and the one institution on this list where EU/EEA students pay tuition: NOK 106,400 a year in 2026-27.

institutions.name: Inland Norway University of Applied Sciences
institutions.englishBachelors: 3 — Game Art and Animation (Hamar), Game Technology (Hamar), Philosophy, Politics and Economics (Lillehammer)
institutions.note: The surprise of the Norwegian list — two game-development degrees and a PPE, all in English, all free for EU/EEA students. Hamar is a recognised Norwegian games-education cluster. INN gained full university status in 2024.

institutions.name: Norwegian School of Economics
institutions.englishBachelors: 1 — BSc in Business, Economics and Data Science
institutions.note: A selective business school — roughly 20% acceptance, triple-crown accredited, and about 40% of students go on exchange. Free for EU/EEA. The EU/EEA window closes 15 February 2027.

institutions.name: Norwegian University of Life Sciences
institutions.note: Home to a veterinary school, and to an English-taught bachelor in International Environment and Development Studies, for an IB student drawn to ESS, biology and global development. With Danish, Norwegian or Swedish A you apply through Samordna opptak by 15 April; without it, directly by 1 December 2026.

institutions.name: University of Oslo
institutions.englishBachelors: 1 — Technology Systems: Science and Engineering (Kjeller campus)
institutions.note: For an IB student without Norwegian there is exactly one English bachelor's door, and it wants every document by 1 December 2026. With Danish, Norwegian or Swedish A, the university's Norwegian-taught bachelor's are open through Samordna opptak.

institutions.name: Nord University
institutions.englishBachelors: 1–2 — BSc Biology (Bodø) confirmed; Acting and Artistic Production listed elsewhere but unconfirmed
institutions.note: The English-taught BSc Biology in Bodø is genuinely distinctive — Arctic and aquatic biology above the Arctic Circle, free for EU/EEA students. Documentation can be extended to 1 July, which helps an IB applicant.

institutions.name: Oslo National Academy of the Arts
institutions.englishBachelors: 1 — Classical Ballet only; the other nine bachelors are taught in Norwegian
institutions.note: A tiny, fiercely selective conservatoire outside the national admission system. Its only English door is Classical Ballet, audition-driven, closing at the end of February.

institutions.name: Norwegian University of Science and Technology
institutions.englishBachelors: None. NTNU states that all undergraduate programmes are taught in Norwegian and require Norwegian proficiency.
institutions.note: Norway's engineering powerhouse and its largest university, with a Nobel-winning neuroscience institute. Every bachelor's is in Norwegian, but Danish, Norwegian or Swedish A at grade 3 or better documents that for Samordna opptak — so it is open to an IB student with one of those who is willing to study in Norwegian.

institutions.name: University of Bergen
institutions.englishBachelors: None in practice. UiB's English filter returns three bachelors, but all three are Norwegian-language degrees with English components.
institutions.note: Known for marine and climate science. Treat it as a master's destination — the bachelor listing in English is misleading.

institutions.name: UiT The Arctic University of Norway
institutions.englishBachelors: None. UiT states it currently offers no bachelor programmes taught in English.
institutions.note: In Tromsø, focused on Arctic and polar research, space science and fisheries — but bachelor entry is closed to non-Norwegian speakers. Master's applications open 1 February 2027.

institutions.name: Norwegian School of Sport Sciences
institutions.englishBachelors: None. Bachelor's programmes are applied for through Samordna opptak; English-taught provision is at master's level and in online courses.
institutions.note: A specialist sport-science university. Bachelor entry goes through Samordna opptak in Norwegian.

institutions.name: University of Stavanger
institutions.englishBachelors: One: Bachelor in Dance. UiS states that all its other undergraduate programmes are taught in Norwegian.
institutions.note: Norway's energy-industry university, in the country's oil capital. Cut its non-EEA fees sharply from August 2026.

institutions.name: Oslo Metropolitan University
institutions.englishBachelors: Unclear — the programme filter indicates one, but it could not be identified. Email international@oslomet.no before assuming.
institutions.note: Large and professionally oriented, with around 20,000 students. Cut its product-design fee for non-EEA students from NOK 418,000 to NOK 95,000 in August 2026.
